say: Clear waves safely with Orb, then look for a Charm pick once you're six, or keep pushing and roam if nobody steps forward.
more: Charm stops dashes and walks the target toward you, so one hit usually decides the fight. Most of what you do is landing it or threatening it.
Spirit Rush gives three dashes, and more on takedowns, so after six you can enter, dodge and leave. Before six you are a safe wave clearer without much kill threat alone.
Later you are the pick maker: catch one person before an objective so the fight starts uneven.
check: Whether minions stand between you and the target, because Charm stops on the first enemy it meets.
breaks: If they stay behind minions all game or you keep missing Charm, stop hunting picks and play as wave clear and peel beside your carry.

more: Spirit Rush has three casts, so you can use one to get an angle for Charm and still keep casts to chase or to get out.
Takedowns give extra recasts, which is why Ahri gets better in fights that turn into a second and third kill.
Your first completed item is the next step up: waves die faster, and that frees time to move before their mid can.
check: Their health, whether their flash and escape are available, and where their jungler was last seen.
breaks: If you use every dash going in and the kill doesn't come, you have no way out. Keep one cast unless the kill is certain.

say: Trade with Orb through the wave when they step up to last hit, or just shove and keep your mana if they outrange you.
more: Orb deals true damage on the way back, so stand where the return path crosses them rather than only aiming the throw.
Fox-Fire gives a short speed burst, useful for dodging a skillshot or stepping in for the returning Orb. Your passive heals you as you kill minions, so farming keeps you topped up.
Save Charm for a trade you are sure of, or for their jungler. Missing it tells them you are harmless for a while.
check: Your mana bar, and whether their main skillshot was just used.
breaks: Against champions who win up close, don't walk up to attack. Farm with Orb from range and wait for six.

more: Spirit Rush lets you arrive from an angle the lane does not expect, and Charm holds the target long enough for teammates to follow.
Leaving on a pushed wave means their mid loses farm to the tower if they follow you, and you lose little if the roam fails.

check: Where the side-lane waves are, and whether their mid can follow you or shove your tower.

more: A Charm landed before the fight starts is worth more than any dive, because the target walks into your whole team.
Each takedown gives another Spirit Rush cast, so start on the target you can actually finish, not the most valuable one.
If their team has several ways to lock you down, your dashes are for dodging those, not for going in.

Void Surge is your dash, Above and Below is the knock-up and slow, and Royal Maelstrom heals you and cuts damage while you slash the lowest-health enemy nearby.
Endless Banquet turns Void coral into your true form, with more health, range and attack speed. That is the state you want to be in for objective fights.

Casting an ability gives temporary attack speed too, so weave spells between attacks rather than saving them.

That makes Bel'Veth better in drawn-out skirmishes than in one quick gank: the longer it goes, the more she gets out of it.

Void Surge closes the gap and Royal Maelstrom finishes, since it targets the lowest-health enemy. A gank on a half-health target is much better than on a full one.

say: Play lane aggressively with your support and turn leads into dragons, or kite back and stack spears if they have more engage than you.
more: Kalista hops a short distance after every attack, so she is always moving while she fights. That makes her good at dodging and at chasing.
Every attack leaves a spear, and Rend rips them all out for damage that grows with each spear. Long trades favor you; single hits do not.
Her whole kit is tied to her bound support: bonus damage when you both hit the same target, and an ultimate that pulls them to you.

more: Fate's Call teleports your bound ally to you, and they then dash to a spot and knock enemies back. With a tanky support that is a strong engage.
Used the other way, it rescues a support who got caught, and their dash can knock the divers off you.
Items matter as well: each one that adds attack speed means more spears in the same fight, and so a bigger Rend.

Spears stack on monsters too, and Rend's damage grows with each one. That gives your team a second finishing blow next to your jungler's smite.
